nodes.name: ERCC4/XPF
nodes.description: ERCC4/XPF is a DNA repair gene associated with xeroderma pigmentosum group F when biallelic pathogenic variants disrupt its function.
evidence: Xeroderma pigmentosum group F (XP-F) is caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the ERCC4/XPF gene.

nodes.name: c.2251-15T>G
nodes.description: c.2251-15T>G is a recurrent deep intronic founder mutation in ERCC4/XPF identified in affected individuals from the Canary Islands.
evidence: We identified a recurrent deep intronic ERCC4 variant, c.2251-15T>G, in affected individuals from the Canary Islands.

nodes.name: xeroderma pigmentosum group F
nodes.description: Xeroderma pigmentosum group F is a disease caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in ERCC4/XPF.
evidence: Xeroderma pigmentosum group F (XP-F) is caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the ERCC4/XPF gene.

nodes.name: antisense oligonucleotide splice correction
nodes.description: Antisense oligonucleotides targeting the aberrant splice acceptor can restore normal ERCC4 splicing in patient-derived fibroblasts.
evidence: Antisense oligonucleotides targeting the aberrant splice acceptor restored normal ERCC4 splicing in patient-derived fibroblasts.

edges.description: The c.2251-15T>G deep intronic variant is located in the ERCC4/XPF gene.
evidence: We identified a recurrent deep intronic ERCC4 variant, c.2251-15T>G, in affected individuals from the Canary Islands.

edges.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants in ERCC4/XPF cause xeroderma pigmentosum group F.
evidence: Xeroderma pigmentosum group F (XP-F) is caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the ERCC4/XPF gene.

edges.description: Antisense oligonucleotide splice correction targets the aberrant splice acceptor created by the deep intronic ERCC4 variant.
evidence: The c.2251-15T>G variant created an aberrant splice acceptor; antisense oligonucleotides targeting the aberrant splice acceptor restored normal ERCC4 splicing in patient-derived fibroblasts.
